findings.evidence: Average.lean:110-144 are each a `simp only [circleAverageTransverse_def]` + `exact Real.circleAverage_*`; only lines 150-160 contain a hand argument. Mathlib has no `circleAverage_eq_zero_of_odd`: grep over upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/CircleAverage.lean lists `circleAverage_neg_radius`, `_abs_radius`, `_const_on_circle`, `_nonneg_of_nonneg` and no odd-function lemma, so the general statement is new work and currently only available at `Transverse`.
findings.fix: Prove `Real.circleAverage_eq_zero_of_odd {f : ℂ → E} (h : ∀ z ∈ Metric.sphere (0:ℂ) |R|, f (-z) = -f z) : Real.circleAverage f 0 R = 0` in `EpsilonEridani/Mathematics/` (the same place `SemilinearIsometryClass.norm_map_of_mem_sphere_zero` was hoisted to), using `Real.circleAverage_neg_radius` and `circleMap 0 (-R) θ = -circleMap 0 R θ`; then make the transverse version a three-line transport exactly like `circleAverageTransverse_const_on_circle`/`_nonneg_of_nonneg`. While doing so, the repeated `fun z hz => _ (SemilinearIsometryClass.norm_map_of_mem_sphere_zero Complex.orthonormalBasisOneI.repr hz)` block (lines 134-136 and 142-144, a third copy would be needed) is worth a single named transport helper.
findings.issue: `circleAverageTransverse_eq_zero_of_odd` is the only lemma in the circle-average section not transported from Mathlib: it rebuilds the argument by hand (rewrite both sides of `_neg_radius` into integral form, `simp_rw [hodd, intervalIntegral.integral_neg, smul_neg]`, then `linear_combination (norm := module) -h` and `simpa`). The fact proved is entirely general — the circle average about 0 of a function odd on `sphere 0 |R|` vanishes — and nothing in it is specific to `Transverse`; the binder rewriting also depends on the exact syntactic shape produced by `circleAverageTransverse_eq_integral`.

summary: Proofs are short, documented, and free of `show`/`change` or undocumented defeq. One exception: the odd-function vanishing argument is the only real reasoning in the file and is done inline at the specialised type, breaking the module's own one-line-transport pattern and keeping a general `Real.circleAverage` fact out of reach.
